description: What is below a point, in one call: seismic zone, nearest active faults, lineaments and recorded earthquakes, rock type (GSI lithology) and landform, aquifer, a permeability class (GLHYMPS, global and coarse), nearby groundwater wells, soil at 0-5, 5-15 and 15-30 cm (ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0: clay, sand, silt, pH, organic carbon, bulk density, CEC, nitrogen, WRB soil group) and the nearest Soil Health Card sample, ground subsidence (cm/yr) in megacities, and tunnels, buried pipelines and cables, mines and caves nearby. Returns a one-line `summary` plus `sections`, each layer with its credit, licence (non-commercial ones flagged) and status (found, none_within_radius, or not_covered where the layer does not reach the point); layers that could not be read are listed in `unavailable`. Example: 'what is under this plot in Delhi?' -> lat: 28.525, lng: 77.085. For a narrow question pass sections (or layers) so ground_at reads only those: one section takes about 0.1 to 0.3 s, against up to 2 s for everything, and the answer is only what was asked ('what seismic zone is this?' -> sections: ["seismic"]; 'is the groundwater safe here?' -> sections: ["groundwater"]; 'soil at this farm' -> sections: ["soil"]). For a broad one ('what is at this point?', a site screening) pass neither and it reads everything. list_layers and get_layer_detail say which section reads a layer (lookups); an unknown section, or a layer the tool does not read, is an error naming the valid ones.

layers.description: Read only these layers (ids, e.g. soilgrids (the SoilGrids raster), seismic_zones, cgwb_aquifers), as well as any sections asked; default all

open_only.description: true leaves out the non-commercial layers (for commercial use); default false

sections.description: Read only these sections (an array, or one comma-separated string); default all

name: ground_at
